::: {#exr-04-the-four-layers-of-a-question-interactive}
## The four layers of a question, interactive

Sort the password-reuse examples to the layer each one belongs to. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "aim",
   "label": "Aim"
  },
  {
   "id": "obj",
   "label": "Objective"
  },
  {
   "id": "rq",
   "label": "Research question"
  },
  {
   "id": "hyp",
   "label": "Hypothesis"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "understand why employees reuse passwords",
   "b": "aim"
  },
  {
   "t": "survey 150 employees; interview 8 of them",
   "b": "obj"
  },
  {
   "t": "which factors are associated with password reuse among SMB employees?",
   "b": "rq"
  },
  {
   "t": "H1: perceived account value is negatively associated with reuse",
   "b": "hyp"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "The aim is the overall intent, objectives are checkable steps, the research question is what the study answers, a hypothesis is a testable predicted answer.",
 "ref": "sec-04-anatomy",
 "reflabel": "Anatomy"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-04-question-types-interactive}
## Question types, interactive

Descriptive, comparative or relationship: sort the questions and templates. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "desc",
   "label": "Descriptive"
  },
  {
   "id": "comp",
   "label": "Comparative"
  },
  {
   "id": "rel",
   "label": "Relationship"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "how widespread is password reuse among SMB employees?",
   "b": "desc"
  },
  {
   "t": "do developers with security training reuse passwords less than those without?",
   "b": "comp"
  },
  {
   "t": "does perceived account value affect password reuse?",
   "b": "rel"
  },
  {
   "t": "how frequent or large is X in group G?",
   "b": "desc"
  },
  {
   "t": "does group A differ from group B on X?",
   "b": "comp"
  },
  {
   "t": "is X associated with Y?",
   "b": "rel"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "The shape of the question already implies the data: a count, a comparison of groups, or a measured association.",
 "ref": "sec-04-question-types",
 "reflabel": "Question types"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-04-the-five-failure-modes-interactive}
## The five failure modes, interactive

Drag each draft question to its failure mode. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "broad",
   "label": "Too broad"
  },
  {
   "id": "triv",
   "label": "Trivial yes/no"
  },
  {
   "id": "nores",
   "label": "Not researchable"
  },
  {
   "id": "double",
   "label": "Double-barreled"
  },
  {
   "id": "assum",
   "label": "Assumption baked in"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "\"How can cyber security be improved?\"",
   "b": "broad"
  },
  {
   "t": "\"Is phishing dangerous?\"",
   "b": "triv"
  },
  {
   "t": "\"Should companies be punished for breaches?\"",
   "b": "nores"
  },
  {
   "t": "\"How do users choose passwords and why do they reuse them?\"",
   "b": "double"
  },
  {
   "t": "\"Why does TypeScript make teams faster?\"",
   "b": "assum"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "A career, not a study; answerable without data; a value judgement; two studies in one; an effect presumed rather than investigated.",
 "ref": "sec-04-from-bad-to-good",
 "reflabel": "From bad to good"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-04-testable-hypotheses-interactive}
## Testable hypotheses, interactive

Select the hypotheses that are testable as stated. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="pick">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "options": [
  {
   "t": "H1: employees with security training reuse fewer passwords than those without",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "H3: perceived account value is negatively associated with reuse",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "H2: the new warning design is better",
   "ok": false
  },
  {
   "t": "Is phishing dangerous?",
   "ok": false
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Testable means two groups or named variables, a measurable outcome and a stated direction; \"better\" has no measure or direction.",
 "ref": "sec-04-worked-examples-and-tables",
 "reflabel": "Hierarchies and hypotheses"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::
